issue.title: fix: add confusable/homograph protection to username validation
issue.body:
## problem

the name server validates usernames against IDNA 2008 rules (punycode encoding, DNS label limits, emoji rejection, ZWJ rejection), but does not protect against cross-script confusable attacks. a user can register a name that is visually identical to an existing name using characters from a different unicode script, and NIP-05 verification will confirm both as legitimate `@divine.video` identities.

example: `matt` (ASCII) vs `mаtt` (Cyrillic а at position 2) are visually indistinguishable but would resolve to different pubkeys. any client displaying a verified checkmark would show both as legitimate.

this was surfaced while reviewing a punycode-encoded registration containing a trademark symbol, which is itself benign but highlighted the gap.

## risk

- identity spoofing via visually identical NIP-05 names
- undermines the trust signal that `name@divine.video` verification provides to clients
- low likelihood today given user count, but the attack is trivial to execute

## approaches (based on browser and platform best practices)

**1. single-script restriction**
reject labels that mix scripts (e.g., Latin + Cyrillic in the same name). this is what Chrome and Firefox do for IDN display. simple to implement, eliminates the highest-impact attack class.

**2. skeleton-based confusable detection (UTS #39)**
apply Unicode Technical Standard #39's skeleton algorithm (NFD + confusable character mapping) at registration time. reject any new name whose skeleton collides with an existing registered name. this is what GitHub-style username systems converge on. more comprehensive than script restriction alone — catches both cross-script and within-script confusables. requires vendoring Unicode confusable data (published by the Unicode Consortium as `confusables.txt`) and keeping it current with Unicode releases, or depending on an npm package that wraps it. the check only runs at registration time, not on NIP-05 lookups.

**3. NFKC normalization before storage**
ensure equivalent unicode representations (e.g., `é` as single codepoint vs `e` + combining accent) are normalized to the same canonical form. prevents "same name, different bytes" collisions. should be applied regardless of which other approach is chosen.

**4. ASCII-only restriction**
restrict NIP-05 names to `[a-z0-9-]` only. eliminates the problem entirely but drops internationalized name support, which the current validation explicitly supports across multiple scripts (CJK, Cyrillic, Arabic, Thai, etc.).

## recommendation

option 4 is untenable — the IDN support is intentional and well-tested. option 1 is a subset of what option 2 provides. recommend implementing **option 2 (skeleton-based confusable detection) + option 3 (NFKC normalization)** to get this right from the start.

also worth considering: an audit of existing registered names for confusable collisions with each other.

## references

- [UTS #39: Unicode Security Mechanisms](https://unicode.org/reports/tr39/) — skeleton algorithm, mixed-script detection, restriction levels
- [Chromium IDN display policy](https://chromium.googlesource.com/chromium/src/+/main/docs/idn.md) — Chrome's "Highly Restrictive" profile
- [RFC 5892 (IDNA 2008)](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc5892) — defines valid codepoints but does not address visual confusability
- current validation: `src/utils/validation.ts`

issue.title: fix(invites): call the real invite redemption endpoint in username claims
issue.body:
## Bug

`src/routes/username.ts:320` calls `POST ${INVITE_FAUCET_URL}/api/invite/redeem`. That endpoint does not exist on the invite-darshan service.

`divine-invite-darshan` exposes `/v1/consume-invite` (and related) under the `/v1/` prefix; the `/api/invite/redeem` path returns 404 from the faucet's route table.

## Impact

Any username-claim flow that requires an invite redemption will fail silently (the code/path treats redemption as a precondition to reservation). If `INVITE_FAUCET_URL` is set in the environment, the redemption call 404s; if it's unset, the branch is skipped. Either way, the redemption side of the flow doesn't happen, and name-server reservations that should be invite-gated are effectively ungated.

## Recommended fix

Update the URL to call the real endpoint (`${INVITE_FAUCET_URL}/v1/consume-invite`) and adjust the request body / auth to match that endpoint's contract. That endpoint requires a NIP-98 auth header signed by the invitee's keypair — if the name-server doesn't have access to the invitee's signer, this redemption path needs an alternative (e.g., a dedicated admin-level endpoint on invite-darshan that consumes a code on behalf of a target pubkey, which would itself be a new feature on invite-darshan).

Alternatively, remove the redemption branch if it's vestigial.

## Origin

Identified during ecosystem audit for divine-invite-darshan PR #39. Flagged because it lives in the invite-code redemption path and silently no-ops today.

comment.body:
@mbradley @NotThatKindOfDrLiz I checked the name-server side, and I don’t think this can be fixed with just a URL change.

The current `/api/username/reserve` flow only has `name`, `email`, and `invite_code`. It doesn’t have the invitee’s pubkey or a NIP-98 signature for the invite service request, so name-server can’t call `/v1/consume-invite` correctly on behalf of the user.

I think we have two realistic options:

1. Add a server/admin endpoint in invite-darshan that name-server can call with the code + target identity.
2. Move invite redemption to the client, where the user can actually sign the NIP-98 request.

If the invite path is no longer intended, we should probably remove it from name-server so it doesn’t look like invite-gating is working when it isn’t.

issue.title: Replace temporary Fastly API token with automation token
issue.body:
the `FASTLY_API_TOKEN` worker secret is currently a personal API token (global scope, expires 2026-08-05) tied to matt's Fastly account. this was set as an immediate fix — the previous token (set by rabble in january) was returning 401 and silently breaking all D1→Fastly KV sync.

we need a Fastly automation token to replace it. automation tokens aren't tied to a user account, so they survive personnel changes. only Fastly superusers can create them.

**requirements:**
- scope: global (KV store writes require it)
- access: all services (KV API is account-level)
- no expiration (or long-lived)
- once created, update the worker secret: `npx wrangler secret put FASTLY_API_TOKEN`

**context:**
- the token is used by the hourly cron reconciliation and the admin backfill endpoint to sync D1 usernames to the `divine-names` Fastly KV store
- also discovered an unused Fastly Compute service `divine-name-sync` (`keqSxRML0NxLxA6jChGqIz`) that rabble set up Dec 28 as a webhook-based sync approach — zero traffic, never wired up. worth deciding whether to decommission it or finish wiring it up as the preferred sync path.

issue.title: Re-point ike.divine.video to original owner (lost via mobile profile-edit bug)
issue.body:
## Context

A bug in the mobile app (now fixed) was silently stripping the `nip05` field from Kind 0 republishes when users edited their profile, which broke the `<handle>.divine.video → pubkey` binding on this server.

- Root cause + reproduction: divinevideo/divine-mobile#4012
- Detailed analysis: divinevideo/divine-mobile#4021
- Fix (merged 2026-05-06): divinevideo/divine-mobile#4022

## Affected user

- Handle: `ike.divine.video`
- Owner pubkey: `npub14mwc76ywjhu4xvfeafc83dwqltnnj9hndn3f44nwdjfas2tv7xlqy9gqkf`
- Reporter: @ike-fyi
- Zendesk ticket: `rabblelabs.zendesk.com/agent/tickets/1684`

ike is an early adopter who originally claimed `ike` and previously had a verified subdomain pointing at his profile. After he edited his profile in the mobile app, the bug republished a Kind 0 without `nip05`, the binding dropped on this server, and the slot was re-claimed by a legacy Vine-import account that holds ~1 video. The in-app `claimUsername` flow (`POST /api/username/claim`) now returns 409 (taken), so he cannot recover it himself.

## Ask

Manually re-point `ike` → `npub14mwc76ywjhu4xvfeafc83dwqltnnj9hndn3f44nwdjfas2tv7xlqy9gqkf` on `names.divine.video`. If the conflict is a duplicate Vine-import claim rather than a fresh user registration, this likely needs to be coordinated with `divine-resurrection` to unwind the legacy assignment cleanly.

## Other potentially-affected users

Anyone who edited their profile on a vulnerable mobile build between the introduction of the bug and the merge of divinevideo/divine-mobile#4022 may have lost their verified handle the same way. Worth a one-time audit for other handles that no longer resolve to the pubkey that originally claimed them.

issue.title: NIP-05 sync verification and admin UI feedback
issue.body:

### Code review

Found 4 issues:

1. **No length cap on `admin_notes`** -- Every other text input in this file is capped (query: 100, tag: 50, reserved_word: 50). Notes accepts an unbounded string to D1. Add a guard like the others, e.g. `if (trimmed && trimmed.length > 5000) return c.json({ ok: false, error: 'Notes too long' }, 400)`.

https://github.com/divinevideo/divine-name-server/blob/ee39248518916781b65ad0426954568c5f03f8dc/src/routes/admin.ts#L223-L225

2. **No audit trail on notes mutation** -- Every other write endpoint in `admin.ts` captures `adminEmail` and records who performed the action (`reserveUsername`, `assignUsername`, `addTag` all pass `createdBy`). The notes endpoint records `updated_at` but not who edited. For a T&S tool, this matters. Simplest fix: add a `console.log` with `adminEmail` so it lands in worker logs. Better: add a `notes_updated_by` column in a migration and pass `adminEmail` through to `updateAdminNotes`.

https://github.com/divinevideo/divine-name-server/blob/ee39248518916781b65ad0426954568c5f03f8dc/src/routes/admin.ts#L216-L236

3. **`pending-confirmation` missing from search `validStatuses`** -- The stats endpoint counts `pending-confirmation` records and the Dashboard shows that count, but admins can't filter search results to that status. Add `'pending-confirmation'` to the `validStatuses` array.

https://github.com/divinevideo/divine-name-server/blob/ee39248518916781b65ad0426954568c5f03f8dc/src/routes/admin.ts#L136-L137

4. **`getUsernameStats` fires 15 separate D1 queries on every dashboard mount** -- Since this is SQLite under the hood, the status counts and metadata counts can each be collapsed into a single query using conditional aggregation:

```sql
SELECT
  COUNT(*) AS all_count,
  SUM(CASE WHEN status = 'active' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS active,
  SUM(CASE WHEN status = 'reserved' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS reserved,
  SUM(CASE WHEN status = 'revoked' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS revoked,
  SUM(CASE WHEN status = 'burned' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS burned,
  SUM(CASE WHEN status = 'pending-confirmation' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS pending_confirmation,
  SUM(CASE WHEN admin_notes IS NOT NULL AND TRIM(admin_notes) != '' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS with_notes,
  SUM(CASE WHEN claimed_at IS NOT NULL AND claimed_at >= ? THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS claimed_7d,
  SUM(CASE WHEN claimed_at IS NOT NULL AND claimed_at >= ? THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS claimed_30d,
  SUM(CASE WHEN updated_at >= ? THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS updated_7d,
  SUM(CASE WHEN updated_at >= ? THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS updated_30d
FROM usernames
```

That collapses 12 of the 15 queries into 1. The remaining 3 (tag counts) need the join table, but can similarly be combined into a single query. Total: 3 queries instead of 15.

https://github.com/divinevideo/divine-name-server/blob/ee39248518916781b65ad0426954568c5f03f8dc/src/db/queries.ts#L675-L699

issue.title: NIP-05 sync verification and admin UI feedback
issue.body:
## Summary

- A user's NIP-05 was not resolving despite the name-server DB showing the record as active with a pubkey assigned. Root cause: the worker's `FASTLY_STORE_ID` secret was set to the wrong store, so every `syncUsernameToFastly` call was writing to a store that divine-router never reads. No error was surfaced anywhere.
- Fixed the secret manually (2026-04-30). This issue covers making the system resilient to this class of failure.

## Changes

**1. Move `FASTLY_STORE_ID` from secret to checked-in config (`wrangler.toml` vars)**
The store ID is a resource identifier, not a credential. Checking it in prevents silent drift and makes it reviewable.

**2. Admin UI: NIP-05 resolution status on username detail page**
After looking up a username, fetch the actual `.well-known/nostr.json` endpoint and show a green/red indicator for whether it resolves. Currently the admin UI shows DB state but has zero visibility into edge resolution.

**3. Admin UI: "Re-sync to Fastly" button**
Trigger `syncUsernameToFastly` for a single username from the detail page. Currently the only options are re-assign (side effects on timestamps/source) or running the reconcile script.

**4. Sync verification in the write path**
After `syncUsernameToFastly` writes a KV entry, read it back to confirm it landed. Log a warning if verification fails. This catches wrong store ID, expired token, or API failures that the current fire-and-forget `waitUntil` silently swallows.

## Context

- divine-router (Fastly Compute) reads from KV store `divine-names` (`gclbp6suv4bjnqpctp2b7n`)
- divine-name-server (CF Worker) writes to whatever `FASTLY_STORE_ID` is set to
- Hourly cron reconciliation also times out at 90K+ users
- Self-service claims fire sync via `waitUntil` (fire-and-forget) with no feedback on failure

issue.title: test: end-to-end coverage for claim → NIP-05 resolution flow
issue.body:
## Context

PR #35 fixed a bug where `revoked_at` wasn't cleared on the ON CONFLICT path during username claims. The fix has unit test coverage (SQL assertions + stateful mock integration tests), but there's no end-to-end test that exercises the full path: HTTP claim request → D1 mutation → Fastly KV sync → NIP-05 resolution.

## Scope

Add route-level tests to `username.test.ts` (or a new e2e test file) that verify:

1. **Claim a name, verify NIP-05 resolves** -- claim via POST, then query `/.well-known/nostr.json?name=<claimed>` and assert the pubkey is returned
2. **Re-claim the same name, verify `revoked_at` is null** -- call claim twice with the same pubkey+name, inspect the DB record to confirm `revoked_at` is not set and NIP-05 still resolves
3. **Switch names, verify old name stops resolving** -- claim name A, then claim name B with the same pubkey. Verify NIP-05 returns B's pubkey and A returns empty
4. **Claim a previously-revoked name** -- revoke a name via admin, then claim it with a new pubkey. Verify NIP-05 resolves to the new pubkey and `revoked_at` is null
5. **Fastly KV sync is called with correct data** -- assert `syncUsernameToFastly` receives `status: 'active'` after claim (already mocked in test suite)

The existing `createMockDB` in `username.test.ts` would need to track `revoked_at` mutations faithfully (similar to `createStatefulMockDB` added in #35). Consider consolidating into a shared test helper.

## Relates to

- #35 (fix: clear revoked_at on username reactivation)

issue.title: fix(invites): call the real invite redemption endpoint in username claims
issue.body:
## Bug

`src/routes/username.ts:320` calls `POST ${INVITE_FAUCET_URL}/api/invite/redeem`. That endpoint does not exist on the invite-darshan service.

`divine-invite-darshan` exposes `/v1/consume-invite` (and related) under the `/v1/` prefix; the `/api/invite/redeem` path returns 404 from the faucet's route table.

## Impact

Any username-claim flow that requires an invite redemption will fail silently (the code/path treats redemption as a precondition to reservation). If `INVITE_FAUCET_URL` is set in the environment, the redemption call 404s; if it's unset, the branch is skipped. Either way, the redemption side of the flow doesn't happen, and name-server reservations that should be invite-gated are effectively ungated.

## Recommended fix

Update the URL to call the real endpoint (`${INVITE_FAUCET_URL}/v1/consume-invite`) and adjust the request body / auth to match that endpoint's contract. That endpoint requires a NIP-98 auth header signed by the invitee's keypair — if the name-server doesn't have access to the invitee's signer, this redemption path needs an alternative (e.g., a dedicated admin-level endpoint on invite-darshan that consumes a code on behalf of a target pubkey, which would itself be a new feature on invite-darshan).

Alternatively, remove the redemption branch if it's vestigial.

## Origin

Identified during ecosystem audit for divine-invite-darshan PR #39. Flagged because it lives in the invite-code redemption path and silently no-ops today.
